user_preferences.primary_goal: A useful independently supported research contribution; original Chiplet application is not mandatory
user_preferences.paper_scope: First doctoral paper, no invented venue/quartile or acceptance guarantee

verdict.overall: The original direction and multi-DMA extension are defensible. Later work drifted from a stable useful problem toward preserving increasingly elaborate candidate mechanisms. Current plan repairs measurement and investment discipline but still prematurely privileges copy-state admission. Retain one bounded problem-driven convergence opportunity; do not automatically resume old mechanisms or start RTL.
verdict.original: Original thesis main.tex:90-125,180-212 treats access-control coverage as a topology premise and evaluates remote PTW cost in an FPGA latency model. It does not experimentally establish real Chiplet P2P security or mandate all later work stay in Chiplets. Shared-IOMMU external interference is a reasonable new question, not a logical consequence or automatic novel contribution.
verdict.earlier_work: E4 no-overlap and autonomous-supply overlap reports justify measurement repair. E2/E3 provide bounded causal evidence; P4M and method88 provide reusable progress measurements and controls. These assets are useful but their sum is not an accepted new method.
verdict.drift: Risk was explicit by September9. Stopping the tested p5 claim was sound. P/N/PN was useful diagnosis, but treating the combination as something that must win is not justified. October7-9 fragmentation/shared-payload/late-output contracts changed the problem without enough independent workload motivation. Concrete failures justify stopping the tested claims, not dismissing whole fields.
verdict.landscape: Literature maps organize adjacent mechanisms and constraints, not a list of proved open problems or six implementation obligations. DMA shared-resource interference, translation/data priority and partition/scheduling interactions have prior work. This limits generic claims, not all useful DMA-specific interface/rule/cost contributions.
verdict.latest_plan: G0-G3, common work and cost accounting are improvements. G0 must permit a bounded baseline-only discriminator before inventing a new rule. The copy-associated observation/gate remains a candidate; no evidence yet makes it the necessary solution. The existing model measures first V issue to last V done and then stops A, so it cannot be used unchanged for common-ready fixed64+64 completion.
verdict.recommended_decision: Keep the platform and shared translation/service interference problem for one finite feasibility pass. Start with the useful failure of a concrete executable simple control under motivated workload constraints. Design the smallest rule/interface only if evidence locates an actionable deficiency. If no useful residual or predictive/cost contribution survives, archive this subproblem and choose an independently motivated adjacent question; do not automatically repurpose it as a characterization paper.

critical_clarifications: New information is one route to a contribution, not a universal requirement; a new use of existing information or a lower-cost implementation can matter if the exact prior art, benefit and complete cost support it.

A same-information controller containing the candidate's full rule is an alternative implementation/ablation, not evidence that the rule was previously published. Best-per-scenario envelopes are explanatory bounds, not a free online baseline.

One-stage-at-a-time DMA frontend WAIT completes the current A copy before ADMIT controls its successor. A previous-copy state is historical; V may still be active. A gate cannot retroactively repair an already promised current-copy request. Candidate must specify which state is timely for which decision.

Fixed64+64 is a legitimate first mechanism microbenchmark, not a deployed application, a deadline workload or sufficient evidence of general usefulness. Do not impose an entire application port before a small discriminator, and do not fabricate constraints to defeat huge pages or preparation.
Do not conflate V/A completion, safety/protocol capability, mechanism novelty and publication contribution. A protocol-correct prototype can still lose to a simple control.
Ten workdays is a proposed management cap, not a scientific theorem or a newly started clock. No need to fill six mechanisms or a large test matrix.
Previous Codex coordination contributed to mechanism-first advancement and overly broad rejection gates. No measured basis exists to quantify wasted time or token savings.
